entries.name: Log-concavity of polynomials arising from equivariant cohomology
entries.abstract: We study the equivariant cohomology classes of torus-equivariant subvarieties of the space of matrices. For a large class of torus actions, we prove that the polynomials representing these classes (up to suitably changing signs) are covolume polynomials in the sense of Aluffi. We study the cohomology rings of complex varieties in terms of Macaulay inverse systems over $\mathbb{Z}$. As applications, we show that under certain conditions, the Macaulay dual generator is a denormalized Lorentzian polynomial in the sense of Brändén and Huh, and we give a characteristic-free extension (over $\mathbb{Z}$) of the result of Khovanskii and Pukhlikov describing the cohomology ring of toric varieties in terms of volume polynomials.

entries.name: Triangle-free graphs with the fewest independent sets
entries.abstract: Given $d>0$ and a positive integer $n$, let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $d$. With an elegant induction, Shearer (1983) tightened a seminal result of Ajtai, Komlós and Szemerédi (1980/1981) by proving that $G$ contains an independent set of size at least $(1+o(1))\frac{\log d}{d}n$ as $d\to\infty$. By a generalisation of Shearer's method, we prove that the number of independent sets in $G$ must be at least $\exp\left((1+o(1))\frac{(\log d)^2}{2d}n\right)$ as $d\to\infty$. This improves upon results of Cooper and Mubayi (2014) and Davies, Jenssen, Perkins, and Roberts (2018). Our method also provides good lower bounds on the independence polynomial of $G$, one of which implies Shearer's result itself. As certified by a classic probabilistic construction, our bound on the number of independent sets is sharp to several leading terms as $d\to\infty$.

entries.name: Structure and asymptotic preserving deep neural surrogates for uncertainty quantification in multiscale kinetic equations
entries.abstract: The high dimensionality of kinetic equations with stochastic parameters poses major computational challenges for uncertainty quantification (UQ). Traditional Monte Carlo (MC) sampling methods, while widely used, suffer from slow convergence and high variance, which become increasingly severe as the dimensionality of the parameter space grows. To accelerate MC sampling, we adopt a multiscale control variates strategy that leverages low-fidelity solutions from simplified kinetic models to reduce variance. To further improve sampling efficiency and preserve the underlying physics, we introduce surrogate models based on structure and asymptotic preserving neural networks (SAPNNs). These deep neural networks are specifically designed to satisfy key physical properties, including positivity, conservation laws, entropy dissipation, and asymptotic limits. By training the SAPNNs on low-fidelity models and enriching them with selected high-fidelity samples from the full Boltzmann equation, our method achieves significant variance reduction while maintaining physical consistency and asymptotic accuracy. The proposed methodology enables efficient large-scale prediction in kinetic UQ and is validated across both homogeneous and nonhomogeneous multiscale regimes. Numerical results demonstrate improved accuracy and computational efficiency compared to standard MC techniques.

entries.name: Hierarchical filtrations of line bundles and optimal algebraic geometry codes
entries.abstract: We introduce \emph{hierarchical depth}, a new invariant of line bundles and divisors, defined via maximal chains of effective sub-line bundles. This notion gives rise to \emph{hierarchical filtrations}, refining the structure of the Picard group and providing new insights into the geometry of algebraic surfaces. We establish fundamental properties of hierarchical depth, derive inequalities through intersection theory and the Hodge index theorem, and characterize filtrations that are Hodge-tight. Using this framework, we develop a theory of \emph{hierarchical algebraic geometry codes}, constructed from evaluation spaces along these filtrations. This approach produces nested families of codes with controlled growth of parameters and identifies an optimal intermediate code maximizing a utility function balancing rate and minimum distance. Hierarchical depth thus provides a systematic method to construct AG codes with favorable asymptotic behavior, linking geometric and coding-theoretic perspectives. Our results establish new connections between line bundle theory, surface geometry, and coding theory, and suggest applications to generalized Goppa codes and higher-dimensional evaluation codes.

entries.name: Absolutely Summing Toeplitz operators on Fock spaces
entries.abstract: For $1\le p<\infty$, let $F^p_\varphi$ be the Fock spaces on ${\mathbb C}^n$ with the weight function $\varphi$ that \(\varphi \in {\mathcal{C}}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right)\) is real-valued and satisfies $ m{ω}_{0} \leq d{d}^{c}\varphi \leq M{ω}_{0} $ for two positive constants \(m\) and \(M\), \({ω}_{0} = d{d}^{c}{\left| z\right| }^{2}\) is the Euclidean Kähler form on \({\mathbb{C}}^{n}\), \({d}^{c} = \frac{\sqrt{-1}}{4}\left( {\bar{\partial } - \partial }\right)\). In this paper, we completely characterize those positive Borel measure $μ$ on ${\mathbb C}^n$ so that the induced Toeplitz operators $T_μ$ is $r$-summing on $F_{\varphi}^{p}$ for $r \ge 1$.

entries.name: PAC Reasoning: Controlling the Performance Loss for Efficient Reasoning
entries.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) have achieved remarkable progress in complex problem-solving tasks. Despite this success, LRMs typically suffer from high computational costs during deployment, highlighting a need for efficient inference. A practical direction is to switch the LRM between thinking and non-thinking modes dynamically. However, such approaches often introduce additional reasoning errors and lack statistical guarantees for the performance loss, which are critical for high-stakes applications. In this work, we propose Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) Reasoning that controls the performance loss under the user-specified tolerance. Specifically, we construct an upper confidence bound on the performance loss and determine a threshold for switching to the non-thinking model. Theoretically, using the threshold to switch between the thinking and non-thinking modes ensures bounded performance loss in a distribution-free manner. Our experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method can save computational budgets and control the user-specified performance loss.

entries.name: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a weak Asplund space
entries.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space, then $X\times\mathbb R$ is also a weak Asplund space. This resolves an open problem posed by D. G. Larman and R. R. Phelps in 1979 (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 20 (1979), 115-127). The proof combines the Banach-Mazur game, properties of maximal monotone operators, and the G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability of Minkowski functionals. Specifically, we introduce an iterative perturbed Minkowski convex cone approximation game method, and establish a theoretical framework to verify the existence of dense differentiability sets for convex functions on product spaces. By relating the properties of convex functions on the base space and the product space via projection mappings, and constructing dense $G_δ$ subsets using sequences of dense open cones, we demonstrate that the product space satisfies the definition of a weak Asplund space.

entries.name: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
entries.abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.

entries.name: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Compact Quantum Groups with Proper Length Functions
entries.abstract: We study the quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of spectral truncations of \(C(G)\), where \(G\) is a coamenable compact quantum group equipped with a proper length function. Using higher-order commutator seminorms, we establish sufficient conditions for the induced Lipschitz seminorms to define compact quantum metric structures. Furthermore, for the Dirac operators associated with the length function, we prove that their spectral truncations converge to the original space in the quantum Gromov--Hausdorff distance. Our results apply to \(SU(N)\), \(SO(N)\), and related examples, including coamenable compact quantum groups of Kac type with polynomial growth.

entries.name: Sophie Germain, mathématicienne extraordinaire: A story stranger than fiction. Sophie Germain, mathématicienne extraordinaire: une histoire plus étrange qu'une fiction
entries.abstract: English: Sophie Germain (1776-1831) is the first woman known for important original research in mathematics, specifically in elasticity theory and number theory. We outline Germain's recently unearthed number theory results on Fermat's Last Theorem, in the context of her life, work, and interactions with Lagrange, Legendre, and Gauss. For two centuries her accomplishment was thought to consist of a single theorem attributed to her by Legendre, the first general result towards proving Fermat's Last Theorem. But recent discoveries in her handwritten manuscripts and correspondence show that she accomplished much more, albeit forgotten. In particular, she had a plan for proving Fermat's Last Theorem in its entirety, and carried this plan far, using then new tools, e.g., congruence, modular primitive roots, and permutations. Français: Sophie Germain (1776-1831) est la première femme connu pour des recherches originales importantes en mathématiques, en particulier en théorie de l'élasticité et en théorie des nombres. Nous exposons les résultats récemment découverts de Germain en théorie des nombres sur le dernier théorème de Fermat, dans le contexte de sa vie, de son oeuvre et de ses interactions avec Lagrange, Legendre et Gauss. Pendant deux siècles, ses résultats ont été considérés comme formant un seul théorème, attribué à elle par Legendre, et qui était le premier résultat général pour démontrer le dernier théorème de Fermat. Mais des découvertes récentes dans ses manuscrits et sa correspondance montrent qu'elle a accompli bien plus, quoique ce fut oublié. En particulier, elle avait un plan pour démontrer dans son intégralité le dernier théorème de Fermat, et elle a mené loin ce plan, utilisant alors de nouveaux outils, par exemple, la congruence, les racines primitives modulaires et les permutations.

entries.name: Detecting causality with the Links--Gould polynomial
entries.abstract: The conjectures of Low and Natario--Tod, and Penrose's question on Arnold's Problem list ask if causality in spacetimes can be formulated in terms of linking of spheres of light rays in the manifold of all light rays. For $(2+1)$-dimensional spacetimes, this link happens in the manifold coverable by a solid torus $S^1\times \mathbb R^2$. This was solved positively by Chernov and Nemirovski, which raises the question of which link invariants can be used to study causality. Chernov, Martin and Petkova proved that Heegaard--Floer and Khovanov homology completely capture causality. Allen--Swenberg conjectured that the Jones polynomial, which is obtained as an alternating Euler characteristic from Khovanov homology, is also sufficient. But they constructed complicated examples of links $\mathrm{AS}(n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ that suggest that the Alexander--Conway polynomial -- which is the Euler characteristic of Heegaard--Floer homology -- is not enough. The Links--Gould polynomial is a quantum invariant that specializes to the classical Alexander--Conway polynomial in two different ways and somewhat surprisingly inherits some of its characteristic classical features. We show that it distinguishes all the Allen-Swenberg links from the link of causally unrelated events and hence detects causality in all known examples where the Alexander--Conway polynomial is not sufficient. This suggests that it may completely capture causality. The work on the categorification of the Links--Gould Polynomial is an ongoing and hard problem, and it is not a subject of this paper. As a corollary, we also compute the Seifert genus of all Allen--Swenberg links.

entries.name: Bichromatic Geometric Spanners
entries.abstract: For an edge-weighted graph $G=(V,E)$ and a stretch parameter $t\geq 1$, a $t$-spanner is a subgraph $H\subseteq G$ such that the shortest path distances in $G$ and $H$ satisfy $δ_H(u,v)\leq t\, δ_G(u,v)$ for all $u,v\in V$. In metric spanners, $V$ is a finite metric space, and $G$ is the complete graph with edge weights corresponding to the distances between the endpoints. When $G$ is the complete graph on $n$ points in the plane, $O(n)$-size $t$-spanners are possible for any $t>1$: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n/\varepsilon)$ edges (i.e., the stretch can be arbitrarily close to 1). When $G=K(R,B)$ is the complete bipartite graph on $n$ bichromatic points in the plane, in general, no spanner construction can guarantee stretch $t<3$ with $o(n^2)$ edges. Bose et al.~(SICOMP 2009) constructed a $(3+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n\log n)$ edges for any constant $\varepsilon>0$. Our main result is a new construction for a $(3+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(\sqrt{1/\varepsilon}\cdot n)$ edges. Eliminating the $O(\log n)$ factor resolves a problem left open for more than 17 years, and raises a new research problem about optimizing the dependence on $\varepsilon$. When off-metric Steiner points are allowed, no Steiner spanner construction can guarantee stretch $t<2$ with $o(n^2)$ edges, and we construct a bipartite Steiner $(2+\varepsilon)$-spanner for $K(R,B)$ with $O(\sqrt{1/\varepsilon}\cdot n)$ edges. We also study (non-Steiner) spanners for $G=K(R,B)$ on $n$ bichromatic points on the real line: In this case, we show that the MST of $K(R,B)$ is a 7-spanner, and we construct a 3-spanner with at most $2n-3$ edges.

entries.name: A Ramanujan Pell K3 Surface and Cube Representations
entries.abstract: We classify all polynomial representations of $K(u)=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3$ as a sum of two cubes over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without an a priori degree bound. The displayed representation is unique up to interchange and independent multiplication by cube roots of unity. On the elliptic K3 surface $y^2=x^3-432K(u)^2$, the resulting eighteen sections are exactly those of minimum positive Shioda height $4/3$. The proof combines an exact root-pairing calculation with the degree-height relation on the genus-four cover $w^3=K(u)$; it does not require the full Mordell-Weil rank. For the rational representations arising from multiples of the displayed section, we determine the reduced degrees and prove strong divisibility of their common denominators, including an exact formula for each primitive part. We also prove nontorsion at every rational parameter and explain the Pell origin of the sextic. The associated integral lattices and symplectic quotient are treated in appendices. All proofs are in characteristic zero.

entries.name: An infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs with a bisimplicial vertex
entries.abstract: We construct an explicit infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs $G_t$, each with a bisimplicial vertex $v_t$ of degree four and a cutvertex. Thus the same family disproves Hoàng's conjectures excluding bisimplicial vertices and clique cutsets from such graphs. For every integer $t\geq1$, the graph $G_t$ has clique number three and satisfies \[ |V(G_t)|=93+30(t-1),\qquad |E(G_t)|=320+104(t-1). \] Deleting $v_t$ gives a perfectly divisible graph $H_t$ with an edge whose endpoints both lie outside the perfect part of every perfect division. This gives a negative answer to the prescribed-vertex question of Hu, Xu and Zhuang. The same graphs answer their second question affirmatively: each $H_t$ is perfectly divisible but not perfectly weight divisible. The cutvertex and weighted consequences were pointed out by Hu, Xu and Zhuang, who also observed that replacing one endpoint of the edge by two adjacent twins gives a minimally nonperfectly divisible graph with a homogeneous set.

entries.name: The M/PH_2/1 Queue: Explicit Distributions, Sojourn Times and Numerical Benchmarks
entries.abstract: Two-phase phase-type ($PH_2$) distributions are among the service-time models used most often in applied queueing, because they capture coefficients of variation above and below one with few parameters. This note collects, in one place and in ready-to-use form, the stationary queue-length distribution $p_n = A_1 r_1^n + A_2 r_2^n$ and the sojourn-time density $f_{W_s}(t) = c_1 e^{α_1 t} + c_2 e^{α_2 t}$ for the $M/E_2/1$, $M/Hypo_2/1$, $M/Hyper_2/1$ and $M/Coxian_2/1$ queues, with every coefficient written in the parameters that a fitting procedure returns. None of these results is new in substance; however, obtaining them from the general theory takes work that each user would otherwise have to repeat. The formulas are obtained from the Pollaczek-Khinchine transforms, related to the matrix-geometric and phase-type representations of the same queues, and verified numerically in 40-digit arithmetic. The note also gives the matrices needed to reproduce the results in standard software, a comparison with the matrix-analytic library BuTools, formulas for tail and threshold quantities and their derivatives, and a worked example calibrated to published surgical-time data.

entries.name: Nonradial stability of an infinite family of self-similar blow-up profiles for the three-dimensional Keller--Segel equation
entries.abstract: The three-dimensional parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel equation admits infinitely many radial self-similar blow-up profiles. Earlier work established radial and nonradial stability for one explicit profile. We study the non-explicit profiles constructed by inner-outer matching and allow perturbations without any symmetry assumption. For each sufficiently large profile index, we prove that the corresponding blow-up dynamics are asymptotically stable along a Lipschitz manifold of initial data. When the blow-up center and scale are allowed to vary, the codimension of this manifold equals the number of intrinsic unstable radial modes. We derive refined inner-outer asymptotics and two-scale estimates for the profiles and analyze the nonlocal, non-self-adjoint linearized operator in each spherical harmonic sector. In the radial sector, a reduced-mass transformation leads to a local Sturm-Liouville problem and gives the exact number of negative eigenvalues. In the $l=1$ sector, we identify the translation modes and exclude any additional unstable spectrum. For every $l\ge 2$, the sharp lower bound on the real part of the spectrum is $1/4$. We then combine the spectral decomposition with modulation equations, higher-order energy estimates, and a finite-dimensional Brouwer argument to obtain the nonlinear stability result.

entries.name: Perturbed Brownian motion reflected at a time-dependent boundary
entries.abstract: Let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion, $x\ge 0,\, ν<1$, and $b:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function locally of finite variation starting from 0. We define the perturbed Brownian motion reflected at the boundary $b$ by establishing strong existence and pathwise uniqueness of a solution to the equation \[ W_t=(1-ν)x+B_t+νM_t(W)+\frac12 L_t^0(W-b), \qquad W_t\ge b(t), \] where $M_t(W):=\sup_{0\le s\le t} W_s$ and the process $L^0(W-b)$ is the semimartingale local time at 0 of the process $W-b$. We give a positive result under condition (PB) on the boundary $b$ : for every $T>0$, the upward increment $\sup_{0\le s<t\le T,\,t-s\le h}(b(t)-b(s))^+ = o(\sqrt{h})$ as $h\downarrow 0$. The proof splits into two regimes: the case $ν<1/2$ is a consequence of the Skorokhod problem in an orthant proved by [Williams 1995], while the case $ν\ge 1/2$ combines a deterministic comparison estimate and a logarithmic upper bound on the number of completed round-trips, following the strategy of [Chaumont and Doney 1999]. For $α\in(0,1/2)$, we also construct an increasing $α$-Hölder boundary for which no continuous adapted solution starting from zero exists for any $ν<1$.

entries.name: Exact Sign Recovery for PCA Connectivity Analysis in Mixture Models
entries.abstract: We study exact sign recovery for PCA connectivity analysis in mixture models with $K$ components, using the projection onto the first $(K-1)$ principal components. For any fixed number of components with affinely independent means, we derive the oracle signal projection explicitly. Under anisotropic sub-Gaussian noise, with a random number of observations in each component, a rowwise eigenspace bound yields a sufficient condition, governed by the weakest signal direction, for recovering all connectivity signs without requiring a bounded condition number of the nonzero signal spectrum. Under isotropic Gaussian noise, when the configuration of the component means is fixed up to scaling and orthogonal transformations, we identify an asymptotically sharp threshold for the signal strength: exact sign recovery succeeds above the threshold and fails below the threshold, with probability tending to one when the signal strength stays a fixed relative distance from the threshold. For an equally weighted regular simplex, we give an explicit sharp cutoff coefficient and show that optimizing the common entrywise threshold improves the coefficient's dependence on the number of components from linear growth to inverse proportionality.

entries.name: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
entries.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$ of rotation numbers. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotation numbers in $I$ is an ellipse. It suffices to assume these caustics at a suitably chosen family of rotation numbers in $I$ with any prescribed rational point of $I$ as its unique accumulation point. The key linear result classifies real $L^2$ displacements with phase-independent orbit sums at every rational rotation number in $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.

entries.name: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
entries.abstract: For Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes, we develop the first sparse-grid finite element discretizations, for dramatically reducing the number of degrees of freedom used in tensor-product finite elements. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. For the three-dimensional Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes, we construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials, exactness and uniform inf-sup stability of associated mixed methods. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we also prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent algebraic convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to tensor-product finite elements.

entries.name: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
entries.abstract: We propose a parametrization-free method that estimates the principal curvatures and principal directions of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$ from the closest point projections of a few random rays, without coordinate charts or local fitting. The projection of a ray induces a curve on the submanifold, which is a geodesic only in special cases, so its curvature is in general not a curvature of the submanifold. The velocities of these curves, however, relate to the derivative of the closest point projection, whose eigenpairs carry the information of the principal curvatures and directions. Finite differences along $d$ rays can estimate them without relying on the normal information at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections, and we provide error bounds. The method extends to submanifolds of any codimension and to point clouds, and experiments confirm the predicted rates in up to $128$ dimensions.

entries.name: Wang's log-Harnack inequality for Markov chains and its applications
entries.abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\varepsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we prove volume doubling property, which extends the work of Guo-Huang-Huang to general weighted setting. We further prove a sharp volume growth and Li-Yau gradient estimates under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ .

entries.name: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
entries.abstract: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\leτ_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.

entries.name: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
entries.abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\fracα{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-ΔS^m = u_0/Γ(1-α)$. Moreover, we show that $t^αu^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $α=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

entries.name: A Geometry-Robust Nečas-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
entries.abstract: Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.

entries.name: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
entries.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, and we call it the Golod threshold for $I$ over $\m$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We also show that when $I$ is homogeneous, under a suitable degree condition, $\m^k I$ is Golod if and only if $k\geq \mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, i.e., once Golodness is achieved, it cannot be lost. In the last section, we work in the setting of a regular local ring of dimension 3, and show that the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this resolves a question posed by Dao and De Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

entries.name: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
entries.abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly. We will also show that two gcd-graphs over the same matrix ring are isospectral if and only if they have the same generating set.

entries.name: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
entries.abstract: Following Gábor Czédli, the \emph{congruence density} of a finite lattice $A$ is $\cd(A)=|\Con A|/2^{|A|-1}$, where $\Con A$ is its congruence lattice and $|A|$ is its number of elements. Czédli proved that density cannot increase under several kinds of sublattice extension and asked whether this holds for every sublattice inclusion. For a sublattice $S$ of $L$, we prove the stronger inequality $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. The proof follows congruence labels along the chains into which prime intervals of $S$ split in $L$. We also prove that $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ if and only if every element of $L-S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of G. Czédli and L.~Szabó relating compatible quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding quasiorder-density results.

entries.name: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
entries.abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials $P\in\Z[T]$ for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over $\Q(x)$ for $k\ge1$. For $R_n(y)\in\Z[y]$ satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to $\Z[y][[x]]$ and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For $q\in \Z$, taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

entries.name: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
entries.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $β>β_c$ and logarithmically fast when $β<β_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $β$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $β$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $β$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

entries.name: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
entries.abstract: We develop the high-dimensional effective dynamics for adaptive, momentum-based variants of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). These effective dynamics are given by a Markov process. They key observation is that the non-Markovianity in the algorithm due to the exponential moving average and preconditioning can be treated using the method of averaging. Our approach applies to a broad class of algorithms including to Adaptive momentum estimation (ADAM), Momentum orthogonalized by Newton-Schultz (MUON), and its variants. It also applies to a broad class of learning tasks, such at tensor PCA, Gaussian projective models, teacher-student networks, and a multi-layer neural network trained on the XOR problem using a hybrid of MUON and ADAM as commonly done in practice. We demonstrate how to this technique can give precise, quantitative comparisons between algorithms. In particular, we find interesting phenomena, such as the cross-over phenomenon where online SGD has better generalization than ADAM early in training until the learning curves cross and ADAM dominates. Furthermore, we prove a version of the Edge of Stability phenomenon. In particular, we introduce an analogue of the infinity Laplacian that sharply characterizes the Edge of Stability.

entries.name: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
entries.abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.

entries.name: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
entries.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given.

entries.name: Stokes Waves in a Finite-Depth Fluid via a Conformal Transformation
entries.abstract: Euler equations for a spatially periodic surface in a two-dimensional fluid of a finite depth are reduced to a system of evolution equations after a conformal transformation. Compared to the previously developed formal approach, we show that the system of evolution equations is complemented by two constraints which determine the new depth in conformal variables and the Bernoulli integration constant. A locally unique continuation of the traveling Stokes waves with respect to the wave speed is studied by using arguments based on the implicit function theorem. We show that the constraints on the traveling wave profile recover the correct small-amplitude expansion of Stokes waves in physical variables. We also prove for the co-periodic stability problem that the real unstable eigenvalues may bifurcate from the zero eigenvalue only at a critical point of the wave energy. Finally, we perform numerical approximations of the wave profiles for both small and large amplitudes and illustrate different bifurcations along the solution family.

entries.name: Betti numbers of powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs
entries.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the Betti numbers of all powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs.

entries.name: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
entries.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $ξ$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $ζ$ of $p$ such that $ |ξ-ζ|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

entries.name: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
entries.abstract: Let $c(Ω)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $Ω\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $λ$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $Δu=0$ in $Ω\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=λ$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(Ω)\ge c(Ω^*)$, where $Ω^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $Ω\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $λ\geμ/R$, where $πR^2=|Ω|$ and $μ\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(Ω)\ge 0.9142\,c(Ω^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(Ω)\ge\max\{\sqrt{θ(Ω)},κ_N\}\,c(Ω^*)$, where $θ(Ω)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $κ_N$ is an explicit constant with $κ_3\approx0.650$ and $κ_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

entries.name: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
entries.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

entries.name: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
entries.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

entries.name: NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
entries.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

entries.name: The Contact Process with Temporary Immunity on $\mathbb{Z}$
entries.abstract: We develop a regeneration scheme for the one-dimensional contact process with temporary immunity, also known as the spatial SIRS process, a non-attractive interacting particle system. The key ingredient is a one-sided space-time shielding mechanism, constructed from infinite infection paths of an auxiliary process. These paths separate the evolution of the infection front from the configuration and graphical history left behind, allowing us to construct regeneration times without relying on attractiveness. The same shielding mechanism also provides coupling arguments for processes started from different initial configurations. Using this approach, we establish a law of large numbers and a functional central limit theorem for the right edge, existence and uniqueness of an invariant law for the process seen from the edge, and complete convergence. We also prove survival from every nonempty finite infected set for sufficiently large immunity-loss rates and derive an explicit extinction criterion.

entries.name: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
entries.abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $π$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

entries.name: Psyquandle Fares
entries.abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

entries.name: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
entries.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

entries.name: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
entries.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

entries.name: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
entries.abstract: Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$. These are precisely the trivial representation and the irreducible normalized parabolic inductions $\one_{n-2}\timesτ$, where $τ$ is an infinite-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$. The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

entries.name: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
entries.abstract: We study the nonlinear Kirchhoff equation on the waveguide manifolds $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n$: \begin{align*} -\left( a+b \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n}|\nabla_{x,y}u(x,y)|^2\,dxdy\right) Δ_{x,y}u+ωu=|u|^αu, \end{align*} where $a,b>0$, $ω\in \mathbb{R}$, $α\in(0,2^*)$. We first establish existence of the normalized ground states when $α\in(0,2^*)$. To precisely characterize the $y$-dependence of ground states, we apply a scaling argument to handle the integral term $ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^n} |\nabla_{x,y} u(x,y)|^2 dxdy$. To this end, we construct two distinct modified energy functionals, through which we establish the $y$-independence and $y$-dependence of the ground states in two specific regimes: $(i)$ $ d + n \leq 4$ and $α\in (0, \frac{8}{d+n})$; $(ii)$ $d = n = 1$ and $α\in (8, \infty)$.

entries.name: Simulated Annealing with Topological Spatial Chunking for De Novo Protein Sequence Design
entries.abstract: The inverse protein folding problem, designing a discrete amino acid sequence that spontaneously folds into a predefined macroscopic structure, remains a phenomenally demanding combinatorial challenge central to synthetic drug discovery. While algorithms like SA offer a baseline approach for navigating dense biomolecular energy landscapes, applying SA heuristics to large sequences is inherently frustrated by exponentially large search spaces and deep local energy minima. This study proposes a scalable sequence design architecture, Topological Spatial Chunking Simulated Annealing, based on a localized, exact-solving heuristic embedded within a global simulated-annealing wrapper. To fundamentally circumvent exponential scaling walls, we deploy a dynamic solver that segments the global molecular target into shallow, k-variable algorithmic windows. Crucially, rather than partitioning natively by sequential 1D chronology, we introduce topological spatial chunking, which dynamically groups discrete variables based on Euclidean spatial proximity to preserve critical non-local thermodynamic correlations. The spatially localized sub-problems are solved deterministically via exact enumeration, while the global traversal is securely regulated by an exterior simulated annealing governor augmented by dynamic reheating and continuous elitism caching. We comprehensively benchmarked this classical architecture on the standard HP biophysical lattice against targeted 20-merA, 25-mer, 50-mer, and 64-mer geometries. Most notably, when evaluating the computationally exhaustive 50-mer and 64-mer topologies, the framework successfully bypassed widely accepted heuristic boundaries. By leveraging deterministic exact solving to vault classical energy traps, the system algorithmically resolved a novel, ultra-dense sequence-packing configuration for the 50-mer, defining a new theoretical global optimum.

entries.name: Mean-field Token Steering
entries.abstract: We consider stochastic token steering through a deep stack of transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for an interacting particle system on the unit sphere, where interactions arise from the attention mechanism. In the mean-field limit, the token population evolves via a controlled integro-partial differential equation where the feedback control acts as a corrective vector field guiding the population toward an aggregate configuration of tokens in the representation space. We deduce the minimum effort control to accomplish this task over a fixed time horizon interpreted as normalized layer depth. We show that the resulting controlled dynamics for the token population can be understood as a mean-field Schrödinger bridge adapted to the sphere geometry. Building on this, we propose a novel generalization of the dynamic Sinkhorn recursion to compute the consistent token evolution. Numerical experiments confirm that the proposed approach achieves exact steering of the token population.

entries.name: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
entries.abstract: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.

entries.name: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
entries.abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

entries.name: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
entries.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

entries.name: Monotonicity properties of ratios of Ferrers and conical functions related to a Riemannian nonlocal eigenvalue problem
entries.abstract: Recently, for a given Riemannian manifold with certain curvature constraints, S. Kajántó and A. Kristály [KK24] formulated a variational problem (on either positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces) and computed the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions in terms of the radii, curvature and weight. Moreover, they conjectured that a saturation phenomenon exists also in the case of positively or negatively curved Riemannian model spaces (not only in the Euclidean case), and this is based entirely on the incompatibility of a system of nonlinear equations involving special functions, like Ferrers functions of the first kind and conical functions of the first kind. In this paper, we provide a partial solution for both positive and negative curvature case.

entries.name: Pólya inequalities on thin planar networks
entries.abstract: We construct thin planar domains on which the Dirichlet and the Neumann Pólya inequalities both hold strictly. For the neighborhoods of a given finite connected embedded polygonal graph (branches and cycles are allowed) there is a single radius threshold below which both inequalities hold for every eigenvalue index. We also show that every nonempty bounded connected open set in the plane can be approximated, in measure and in the Hausdorff distance, by smooth simply connected domains satisfying both inequalities. Along the same sequence, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue tends to infinity, while each Neumann eigenvalue of fixed positive index tends to zero. In the special case of rectangular frames our estimates lead to explicit sufficient conditions, with no restriction on the aspect ratio.

entries.name: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
entries.abstract: We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $ν$-Schur functions. In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $ν$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data. Finally, we introduce $ν$-inner functions - $ν$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $ν$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $ν$-inner functions are dense in the $ν$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

entries.name: Intersection Cuts for Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programs via Decision-Diagram-Free Sets
entries.abstract: We introduce a novel decision-diagram-based framework for generating intersection cuts to strengthen polyhedral relaxations of bounded mixed-integer nonlinear programs (MINLPs) with general nonlinear constraints. Building on decision diagrams (DDs) that provide outer approximations of MINLP feasible regions, we propose the concept of DD-free sets, which are convex regions whose interiors do not intersect the sets represented by the DDs. By exploiting the underlying graphical structure, we develop efficient methods for constructing these regions without requiring restrictive assumptions on the functional form of nonlinear constraints or access to distance oracles. We investigate the maximality properties of DD-free sets and devise algorithms for obtaining maximal forbidden regions within several structured classes. The resulting intersection cuts exploit geometric information retained in DD representations, enabling further strengthening of relaxations beyond what can be achieved through conventional DD-based convexification. We also introduce interval DDs to facilitate the representation of general nonlinear constraints and establish convergence results for intersections of constraint-specific DDs, providing a theoretical foundation for their integration into global optimization frameworks. Computational experiments on challenging open instances from MINLPLib, encompassing a broad range of nonlinear and nonconvex structures, demonstrate that the proposed approach can substantially improve dual bounds and achieve greater optimality-gap closure than state-of-the-art global optimization solvers. These findings highlight the potential of exploiting graphical representations of infeasible regions to develop stronger cutting planes for general MINLPs.

entries.name: Bayesian Inference for Multivariate Stable Distributions via LePage Representation with von Mises -- Fisher Spectral Measure
entries.abstract: We develop Bayesian inference for multivariate $α$-stable distributions with von Mises--Fisher spectral measure, motivated by the hitting distribution of Brownian motion on the unit sphere. Inference proceeds via a LePage-type series representation with latent radial, spectral, and Poisson components; truncation bias is absorbed through a Gaussian error term, yielding a likelihood that is smooth in $α\in(0,2)$ with no special treatment at the Cauchy boundary $α=1$. The stability index $α$, spectral concentration $κ$, mean direction $η$, and spectral mass $Γ_\infty$ are estimated jointly by Markov chain Monte Carlo. At the Gaussian boundary $α\to 2$, the limiting covariance matrix equals twice the second moment matrix of the spectral measure, with explicit parametric form determined by $η$ and $κ$; in particular, the anisotropy of the limiting Gaussian distribution is controlled solely by the spectral concentration $κ$. Simulation across $α\in[0.25, 1.99]$ confirms reliable recovery of all parameters.

entries.name: Learning the Average Dose-Response Function with a Right-Censored Treatment
entries.abstract: This paper considers estimation and inference for the average dose-response function under right-censored treatment duration and missing outcomes for censored units. Using the duration lower bounds provided by censored records, we construct a novel multiply robust estimator through augmented local estimating equations. Under suitable regularity conditions, the estimator remains consistent when any two of the outcome regression, treatment density, and censoring survival function are consistently estimated. We establish its convergence rate and asymptotic distribution within a cross-fitting framework under appropriate conditions on nuisance estimation. To address local smoothing bias that can distort confidence interval coverage, we further develop a debiased estimator that supports asymptotically valid pointwise inference without undersmoothing. Under additional uniform conditions, we construct simultaneous confidence bands using a Gaussian multiplier bootstrap. Simulation studies evaluate estimation accuracy, the validity of pointwise and uniform inference, and robustness to nuisance model misspecification. A semi-synthetic study calibrated to NHANES illustrates the proposed methods in a setting with a known dose-response function.

entries.name: Martingale and signed diffusive optimal transport: geodesics and gradient flows
entries.abstract: In signed diffusive transport, a path of probability densities $ρ_t$ on the circle and a momentum $m_t$ satisfy $\partial_tρ=\partial_{xx}m$, and the cost of the path is the action $\int_0^1\int m^2/(2ρ)\,dx\,dt$. The diffusivity $m/ρ$ is an unknown of this variational problem and can take either sign. On the real line, the constraint $m\ge0$ gives the martingale Benamou-Brenier problem of Huesmann and Trevisan. We study geodesics and minimizing movements, which discretize gradient flows. For signed geodesics, we prove the $Γ$-convergence of the time-discrete problems for all probability endpoints, and of the fully discrete Fourier-grid problems as the space and time meshes tend to zero independently, without a positive lower bound on the densities. For a modified Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme on the torus, we prove convergence along subsequences to a weak solution of a fourth-order equation, the Derrida-Lebowitz-Speer-Spohn equation for the entropy in dimension one, under the assumption that the densities of the scheme stay above a positive constant on every finite time interval. In dimension one, the normalized minimum values of a discretization with nonnegative momentum and of a discretization by martingale couplings with a fourth-moment cost converge to the same martingale transport cost, and we identify the limit of the minimizing movements with nonnegative momentum for potential energies with bounded second and third derivatives. We compute geodesics and modified JKO trajectories by Douglas-Rachford splitting and by an interior-point method, and bound the optimization errors of selected solutions by dual lower bounds evaluated in interval arithmetic. The computed geodesics approach zero density near the points where the diffusivity changes sign, and along computed trajectories of the modified JKO scheme the density minimum can fall below its initial value.

entries.name: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
entries.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author.

entries.name: Holomorphic vector fields and rationality
entries.abstract: We prove Carrell's conjecture that a smooth complex projective variety with a holomorphic vector field having a nonempty finite zero set is rational. The proof uses slices for projective additive group actions and a birational invariant in the dimension-graded Grothendieck ring. For a vector field with one zero, we bound the second Betti number by the dimension of the kernel of the linear part at that zero. A multiplicative group that normalizes the additive action with a nontrivial character gives a product formula for the Betti numbers and a sharp upper bound for the Euler characteristic. We classify smooth projective surfaces admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero. Among smooth projective threefolds of Picard number one admitting a holomorphic vector field with exactly one zero, there are five isomorphism types.

entries.name: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
entries.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

entries.name: Poisson structure and Integrability of a Hamiltonian flow for the inhomogeneous six-vertex model
entries.abstract: We compute the action-angle variables for a Hamiltonian flow of the inhomogeneous six-vertex model, from a formulation introduced in a 2022 work due to Keating, Reshetikhin, and Sridhar, hence confirming a conjecture of the authors as to whether the Hamiltonian flow is integrable. To demonstrate that such an integrability property of the Hamiltonian holds from the action-angle variables, we make use of previous methods for studying Hamiltonian systems, implemented by Faddeev and Takhtajan, in which it was shown that integrability of a Hamiltonian system holds for the nonlinear Schrodinger's equation by computing action-angle variables from the Poisson bracket, which is connected to the analysis of entries of the monodromy and transfer matrices. For the inhomogeneous six-vertex model, an approach for computing the action-angle variables is possible through formulating several relations between entries of the quantum monodromy, and transfer, matrices, which can be not only be further examined from the structure of $L$ operators, but also from computing several Poisson brackets parameterized from entries of the monodromy matrix.

entries.name: Tilted Solid-On-Solid is liquid: scaling limit of SOS with a potential on a slope
entries.abstract:
The $(2+1)$D Solid-On-Solid (SOS) model famously exhibits a roughening transition: on an $N	imes N$ torus with the height at the origin rooted at $0$, the variance of $h(x)$, the height at $x$, is $O(1)$ at large inverse-temperature $β$, vs $\asymp \log |x|$ at small $β$ (as in the Gaussian free field (GFF)). The former--rigidity at large $β$--is known for a wide class of $|
ablaφ|^p$ models ($p=1$ being SOS) yet is believed to fail once the surface is on a slope (tilted boundary conditions). It is conjectured that the slope would destabilize the rigidity and induce the GFF-type behavior of the surface at small $β$. The only rigorous result on this is by Sheffield '05: for these models of integer height functions, if the slope $θ$ is irrational, then Var$(h(x))	o\infty$ with $|x|$ (with no known quantitative bound). We study a family of SOS surfaces at a large enough fixed $β$, on an $N	imes N$ torus with a nonzero boundary condition slope $θ$, perturbed by a potential $V$ on an $ε_β$-fraction of sites (arbitrarily small). Our main result is (a) the measure on the height gradients $
abla h$ has a limit $μ_\infty$ as $N	o\infty$; and (b) the scaling limit of a sample from $μ_\infty$ converges to a full plane GFF. In particular, we recover the asymptotics Var$(h(x))\sim c\log|x|$. To our knowledge, this is the first example of a tilted $|
ablaφ|^p$ model, or a perturbation thereof, where the limit is recovered at large $β$. The proof looks at random monotone surfaces that approximate the SOS surface, and shows that (i) these form a weakly interacting dimer model, and (ii) the renormalization framework of Giuliani, Mastropietro and Toninelli '17 leads to the GFF limit. New ingredients are needed in both parts, including a nontrivial extension of [GMT17] from finite interactions to ones with exponential decay in the radius.

entries.name: Stabilities of the Kleitman diameter theorem
entries.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of subsets of $[n]$. The diameter of $\mathcal{F}$ is defined as the maximum size of the symmetric difference between any two of its members. Resolving a conjecture of Erdős, Kleitman determined the maximum size of a family with fixed diameter. Specifically, if $2\leq s\leq n-2$ and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq2^{[n]}$ is a family with diameter $s$, then for $s=2d$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i}$; for $s=2d+1$, $|\mathcal{F}|\le \sum_{i=0}^d {n \choose i} + {n-1 \choose d}$. This result, known as the Kleitman diameter theorem, generalizes both the Katona union theorem and the Erdős--Ko--Rado theorem. In 2017, Frankl provided a complete characterization of the extremal families for Kleitman's theorem and established a stability result. In this paper, we determine the extremal families for Frankl's theorem and prove a further stability result of Kleitman's theorem. This solves a recent problem proposed by Li and Wu and provides the second stability for the Kleitman diameter theorem.

entries.name: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
entries.abstract: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.

entries.name: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
entries.abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,Σ_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $Σ_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(Σ)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(Σ)$. We also introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}^d(Σ)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(Σ)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(Σ)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(Σ)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(Σ)$ for every triangulable $Σ_{g,p}$ other than $Σ_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(Σ_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $Σ_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.

entries.name: Automorphism groups of solvable groups of finite abelian ranks
entries.abstract: This paper gives a new explicit construction of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull for virtually solvable groups $Γ$ of finite abelian ranks, taking into account the spectrum $S$ of the group $Γ$. As an application, we make a detailed study of the structure of $Aut(Γ)$ in the finitely generated case and show that a number of natural subgroups are $S$-arithmetic under the condition that $Fitt(Γ)$ is $S$-arithmetic. We then proceed by demonstrating that $Out(Γ)$ has a $S$-arithmetic image in the group of algebraic outer automorphisms of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull. We finish by discussing further applications of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull towards an open conjecture by Nekrashevych and Pete and topological fixed point theory.

entries.name: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a weak Asplund space
entries.abstract: In this paper, we prove that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space, then $X\times\mathbb R$ is also a weak Asplund space. This resolves an open problem posed by D. G. Larman and R. R. Phelps in 1979 (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 20 (1979), 115-127). The proof combines the Banach-Mazur game, properties of maximal monotone operators, and the G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability of Minkowski functionals. Specifically, we introduce an iterative perturbed Minkowski convex cone approximation game method, and establish a theoretical framework to verify the existence of dense differentiability sets for convex functions on product spaces. By relating the properties of convex functions on the base space and the product space via projection mappings, and constructing dense $G_δ$ subsets using sequences of dense open cones, we demonstrate that the product space satisfies the definition of a weak Asplund space.

entries.name: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
entries.abstract: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators.
