This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.

papers.name: Bichromatic Geometric Spanners
papers.abstract: For an edge-weighted graph $G=(V,E)$ and a stretch parameter $t\geq 1$, a $t$-spanner is a subgraph $H\subseteq G$ such that the shortest path distances in $G$ and $H$ satisfy $δ_H(u,v)\leq t\, δ_G(u,v)$ for all $u,v\in V$. In metric spanners, $V$ is a finite metric space, and $G$ is the complete graph with edge weights corresponding to the distances between the endpoints. When $G$ is the complete graph on $n$ points in the plane, $O(n)$-size $t$-spanners are possible for any $t>1$: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a $(1+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n/\varepsilon)$ edges (i.e., the stretch can be arbitrarily close to 1). When $G=K(R,B)$ is the complete bipartite graph on $n$ bichromatic points in the plane, in general, no spanner construction can guarantee stretch $t<3$ with $o(n^2)$ edges. Bose et al.~(SICOMP 2009) constructed a $(3+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(n\log n)$ edges for any constant $\varepsilon>0$. Our main result is a new construction for a $(3+\varepsilon)$-spanner with $O(\sqrt{1/\varepsilon}\cdot n)$ edges. Eliminating the $O(\log n)$ factor resolves a problem left open for more than 17 years, and raises a new research problem about optimizing the dependence on $\varepsilon$. When off-metric Steiner points are allowed, no Steiner spanner construction can guarantee stretch $t<2$ with $o(n^2)$ edges, and we construct a bipartite Steiner $(2+\varepsilon)$-spanner for $K(R,B)$ with $O(\sqrt{1/\varepsilon}\cdot n)$ edges. We also study (non-Steiner) spanners for $G=K(R,B)$ on $n$ bichromatic points on the real line: In this case, we show that the MST of $K(R,B)$ is a 7-spanner, and we construct a 3-spanner with at most $2n-3$ edges.

papers.name: A Ramanujan Pell K3 Surface and Cube Representations
papers.abstract: We classify all polynomial representations of $K(u)=(1-13u+26u^2)^3+(6+182u^2)^3$ as a sum of two cubes over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without an a priori degree bound. The displayed representation is unique up to interchange and independent multiplication by cube roots of unity. On the elliptic K3 surface $y^2=x^3-432K(u)^2$, the resulting eighteen sections are exactly those of minimum positive Shioda height $4/3$. The proof combines an exact root-pairing calculation with the degree-height relation on the genus-four cover $w^3=K(u)$; it does not require the full Mordell-Weil rank. For the rational representations arising from multiples of the displayed section, we determine the reduced degrees and prove strong divisibility of their common denominators, including an exact formula for each primitive part. We also prove nontorsion at every rational parameter and explain the Pell origin of the sextic. The associated integral lattices and symplectic quotient are treated in appendices. All proofs are in characteristic zero.

papers.name: An infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs with a bisimplicial vertex
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit infinite family of minimally nonperfectly divisible graphs $G_t$, each with a bisimplicial vertex $v_t$ of degree four and a cutvertex. Thus the same family disproves Hoàng's conjectures excluding bisimplicial vertices and clique cutsets from such graphs. For every integer $t\geq1$, the graph $G_t$ has clique number three and satisfies \[ |V(G_t)|=93+30(t-1),\qquad |E(G_t)|=320+104(t-1). \] Deleting $v_t$ gives a perfectly divisible graph $H_t$ with an edge whose endpoints both lie outside the perfect part of every perfect division. This gives a negative answer to the prescribed-vertex question of Hu, Xu and Zhuang. The same graphs answer their second question affirmatively: each $H_t$ is perfectly divisible but not perfectly weight divisible. The cutvertex and weighted consequences were pointed out by Hu, Xu and Zhuang, who also observed that replacing one endpoint of the edge by two adjacent twins gives a minimally nonperfectly divisible graph with a homogeneous set.

papers.name: Machine learning the arithmetic of Boyd's Mahler measure conjectures
papers.abstract: Boyd conjectured that the Mahler measure of $P_k(x,y)=x+y+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+k$ for $k$ an integer, is given by $r_kL'(E_k,0)$, where $E_k$ is the elliptic curve associated to the zero locus of $P_k$ and $r_k$ is a rational number. We study various arithmetic properties of $r_k$ using a dataset containing the first $250{,}000$ values of $k$, combining large-scale statistical analysis assisted by \textsc{Claude} with transformer-based experiments carried out using Axolver. We recover Boyd's observation that, apart from a few exceptions, $r_k$ is the reciprocal of an integer. The size of this integer is governed by the conductor of the elliptic curve. Moreover, its $p$-adic valuations display markedly different behavior according to the prime. For $p\geq5$, the observed frequencies of $v_p(r_k)=-m$, for $m\geq1$, are close to $p^{-m}$. At $p=5$, the agreement improves substantially when we restrict to curves with good reduction at $5$. For the primes $2$ and $3$, however, we find additional arithmetic structure involving congruence conditions on $k$ and the primes of bad reduction of $E_k$. Although the neural networks do not predict $r_k$ exactly, they recover significant information about its magnitude and valuations. In particular, the experiments at the prime $2$ suggest predictive relationships within the computed range that are not fully captured by the explicit predictor obtained from our statistical analysis.

papers.name: The M/PH_2/1 Queue: Explicit Distributions, Sojourn Times and Numerical Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Two-phase phase-type ($PH_2$) distributions are among the service-time models used most often in applied queueing, because they capture coefficients of variation above and below one with few parameters. This note collects, in one place and in ready-to-use form, the stationary queue-length distribution $p_n = A_1 r_1^n + A_2 r_2^n$ and the sojourn-time density $f_{W_s}(t) = c_1 e^{α_1 t} + c_2 e^{α_2 t}$ for the $M/E_2/1$, $M/Hypo_2/1$, $M/Hyper_2/1$ and $M/Coxian_2/1$ queues, with every coefficient written in the parameters that a fitting procedure returns. None of these results is new in substance; however, obtaining them from the general theory takes work that each user would otherwise have to repeat. The formulas are obtained from the Pollaczek-Khinchine transforms, related to the matrix-geometric and phase-type representations of the same queues, and verified numerically in 40-digit arithmetic. The note also gives the matrices needed to reproduce the results in standard software, a comparison with the matrix-analytic library BuTools, formulas for tail and threshold quantities and their derivatives, and a worked example calibrated to published surgical-time data.

papers.name: The Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem for odd wheels: Resolving a conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem, which asks for the maximum adjacency spectral radius over graphs with a fixed number of edges that forbid a prescribed subgraph. We settle an open conjecture due to Yu, Li and Peng for odd wheel graphs $W_{2k+1}$. A striking dichotomy appears in the extremal configurations: the forbidden-$W_5$ case and the general case $k\ge 3$ rely on identical stability and dense-core reductions but produce completely different extremal graphs. For sufficiently large size $m$, we derive sharp spectral inequalities and give complete characterizations for graphs achieving equality. Our approach combines the edge-spectral stability theorem with the dense-core method and residual-function analysis. Beyond solving the target conjecture, the developed framework provides a systematic approach for edge-spectral Turán problems and implies several known results for odd cycles, friendship graphs and odd fans. Directions for future research on edge-spectral supersaturation are also discussed.

papers.name: On Samuels' Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $0\leqμ_1\leq\cdots\leqμ_n$ and let $λ>\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=μ_i$, and write $D_i := λ-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}μ_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<λ\right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{μ_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

papers.name: On the gonality of Kneser graphs
papers.abstract: The Kneser graphs $\text{KG}(n,k)$ are a classically studied family of graphs. One known invariant of graphs is gonality (also called divisorial gonality), which is the minimum degree of a rank 1 divisor on the graph. Using known bounds on gonality of simple, connected graphs, one may obtain that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is bounded above by $\binom{n-1}{k}$. In 2014, Harvey and Wood showed that the treewidth (a lower bound on gonality) for $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is $\binom{n-1}{k}-1$ for $n\geq 4k^2-3k+2$. In this paper, using scramble number, another lower bound on gonality, we improve this polynomial bound and show that the gonality of $\text{KG}(n,k)$ is exactly $\binom{n-1}{k}$ for $n\geq \frac{3k^2+k+2}{2}$, and conjecture an even stricter polynomial bound using the uniform edge scramble. We then extend our argument to the family of generalized Kneser Graphs, computing the scramble number and gonality using the same polynomial bound.

papers.name: Transverse Analytic Envelopes and the Baum--Bott Rationality Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study holomorphic first integrals near singular leaves through transverse analytic envelopes. For diagonal actions these are normal toric quotients, and complete semiglobal integrability along singular orbits with independent support weights is equivalent to maximal resonance rank and finite monodromy. For commuting fields in convergent simultaneous Poincaré--Dulac normal form, induced derivations determine the first-integral algebra. Labelled quotients and logarithmic residues reconstruct weights at maximal rank; Grassmannians describe the ambiguity otherwise. Polynomial examples show losses invisible to prescribed finite jets. For the Baum--Bott rationality conjecture, we prove rationality and an explicit residue formula for smooth compact singular components with product charts and a common invertible semisimple transverse linear part of maximal resonance rank. Equivariant cohomology gives higher-degree vanishing for affine diagonal torus actions, including intersecting singular strata.

papers.name: Nonradial stability of an infinite family of self-similar blow-up profiles for the three-dimensional Keller--Segel equation
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel equation admits infinitely many radial self-similar blow-up profiles. Earlier work established radial and nonradial stability for one explicit profile. We study the non-explicit profiles constructed by inner-outer matching and allow perturbations without any symmetry assumption. For each sufficiently large profile index, we prove that the corresponding blow-up dynamics are asymptotically stable along a Lipschitz manifold of initial data. When the blow-up center and scale are allowed to vary, the codimension of this manifold equals the number of intrinsic unstable radial modes. We derive refined inner-outer asymptotics and two-scale estimates for the profiles and analyze the nonlocal, non-self-adjoint linearized operator in each spherical harmonic sector. In the radial sector, a reduced-mass transformation leads to a local Sturm-Liouville problem and gives the exact number of negative eigenvalues. In the $l=1$ sector, we identify the translation modes and exclude any additional unstable spectrum. For every $l\ge 2$, the sharp lower bound on the real part of the spectrum is $1/4$. We then combine the spectral decomposition with modulation equations, higher-order energy estimates, and a finite-dimensional Brouwer argument to obtain the nonlinear stability result.

papers.name: Perturbed Brownian motion reflected at a time-dependent boundary
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a standard Brownian motion, $x\ge 0,\, ν<1$, and $b:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous function locally of finite variation starting from 0. We define the perturbed Brownian motion reflected at the boundary $b$ by establishing strong existence and pathwise uniqueness of a solution to the equation \[ W_t=(1-ν)x+B_t+νM_t(W)+\frac12 L_t^0(W-b), \qquad W_t\ge b(t), \] where $M_t(W):=\sup_{0\le s\le t} W_s$ and the process $L^0(W-b)$ is the semimartingale local time at 0 of the process $W-b$. We give a positive result under condition (PB) on the boundary $b$ : for every $T>0$, the upward increment $\sup_{0\le s<t\le T,\,t-s\le h}(b(t)-b(s))^+ = o(\sqrt{h})$ as $h\downarrow 0$. The proof splits into two regimes: the case $ν<1/2$ is a consequence of the Skorokhod problem in an orthant proved by [Williams 1995], while the case $ν\ge 1/2$ combines a deterministic comparison estimate and a logarithmic upper bound on the number of completed round-trips, following the strategy of [Chaumont and Doney 1999]. For $α\in(0,1/2)$, we also construct an increasing $α$-Hölder boundary for which no continuous adapted solution starting from zero exists for any $ν<1$.

papers.name: Exact Sign Recovery for PCA Connectivity Analysis in Mixture Models
papers.abstract: We study exact sign recovery for PCA connectivity analysis in mixture models with $K$ components, using the projection onto the first $(K-1)$ principal components. For any fixed number of components with affinely independent means, we derive the oracle signal projection explicitly. Under anisotropic sub-Gaussian noise, with a random number of observations in each component, a rowwise eigenspace bound yields a sufficient condition, governed by the weakest signal direction, for recovering all connectivity signs without requiring a bounded condition number of the nonzero signal spectrum. Under isotropic Gaussian noise, when the configuration of the component means is fixed up to scaling and orthogonal transformations, we identify an asymptotically sharp threshold for the signal strength: exact sign recovery succeeds above the threshold and fails below the threshold, with probability tending to one when the signal strength stays a fixed relative distance from the threshold. For an equally weighted regular simplex, we give an explicit sharp cutoff coefficient and show that optimizing the common entrywise threshold improves the coefficient's dependence on the number of components from linear growth to inverse proportionality.

papers.name: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
papers.abstract: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.

papers.name: Four colours are needed for closed-neighbourhood conflict-free colouring of planar graphs
papers.abstract: A colouring of the vertices of a graph is conflict-free with respect to closed neighbourhoods if every closed neighbourhood contains a colour that appears on exactly one of its vertices. The colouring need not be proper. Every planar graph has such a colouring with four colours. Fabrici, Lužar, Rindošová and Soták [Proper conflict-free and unique-maximum colorings of planar graphs with respect to neighborhoods, \emph{Discrete Appl.\ Math.}\ \textbf{324} (2023) 80--92] conjectured that three colours always suffice. We disprove this conjecture. We give a simple gadget construction that turns every planar graph of chromatic number four into a planar graph with no conflict-free colouring with three colours. This also shows that it is NP-complete to decide whether three colours suffice for a planar graph. We also give a critical planar graph on $25$ vertices and $51$ edges that needs four colours, with a proof that can be checked by hand. Finally, we give an infinite family of plane triangulations that need four colours, and an infinite family of critical examples.

papers.name: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
papers.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$ of rotation numbers. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotation numbers in $I$ is an ellipse. It suffices to assume these caustics at a suitably chosen family of rotation numbers in $I$ with any prescribed rational point of $I$ as its unique accumulation point. The key linear result classifies real $L^2$ displacements with phase-independent orbit sums at every rational rotation number in $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations.

papers.name: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
papers.abstract: For Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes, we develop the first sparse-grid finite element discretizations, for dramatically reducing the number of degrees of freedom used in tensor-product finite elements. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. For the three-dimensional Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes, we construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials, exactness and uniform inf-sup stability of associated mixed methods. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we also prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent algebraic convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to tensor-product finite elements.

papers.name: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
papers.abstract: We propose a parametrization-free method that estimates the principal curvatures and principal directions of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$ from the closest point projections of a few random rays, without coordinate charts or local fitting. The projection of a ray induces a curve on the submanifold, which is a geodesic only in special cases, so its curvature is in general not a curvature of the submanifold. The velocities of these curves, however, relate to the derivative of the closest point projection, whose eigenpairs carry the information of the principal curvatures and directions. Finite differences along $d$ rays can estimate them without relying on the normal information at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections, and we provide error bounds. The method extends to submanifolds of any codimension and to point clouds, and experiments confirm the predicted rates in up to $128$ dimensions.

papers.name: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.name: Wang's log-Harnack inequality for Markov chains and its applications
papers.abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\varepsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\leκm_-$. Under the Bakry--Émery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we prove volume doubling property, which extends the work of Guo-Huang-Huang to general weighted setting. We further prove a sharp volume growth and Li-Yau gradient estimates under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ .

papers.name: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
papers.abstract: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\leτ_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.

papers.name: Large-Time Behavior and Asymptotic Profiles for Time-Fractional Nonlinear Diffusion Equations via Entropy Methods
papers.abstract: We investigate the large-time behavior of nonnegative solutions to the time-fractional nonlinear diffusion equation $\partial_t^α(u-u_0) = Δu^m$, $0<α<1$, $m>0$, in a bounded domain with the homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that the rescaled solution $t^{\fracα{m}}u$ converges as $t\to\infty$ to an asymptotic profile $S$ characterized by $-ΔS^m = u_0/Γ(1-α)$. Moreover, we show that $t^αu^m$ converges to $S^m$, which admits an explicit representation in terms of the Green function and the initial datum. In contrast to the classical case $α=1$, the asymptotic profile depends explicitly on the initial datum.

papers.name: A Geometry-Robust Nečas-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.

papers.name: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.name: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

papers.name: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with $°F=4$ and $n=221$.In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=26$. We also show that $16$ existential unknowns suffice under the $abc$-conjecture.

papers.name: Rational isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

papers.name: Golod thresholds of ideals and products of ideals in dimension 3
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a proper ideal in a standard graded polynomial ring $P$ with homogeneous maximal ideal $\m$. We show that there exists $k_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\m^kI$ is Golod for all $k\geq k_0$. The smallest such $k_0$ is denoted $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, and we call it the Golod threshold for $I$ over $\m$. We give an explicit formula for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ in the case when $I$ is a monomial complete intersection and bounds for $\mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$ for other classes of ideals. We also show that when $I$ is homogeneous, under a suitable degree condition, $\m^k I$ is Golod if and only if $k\geq \mathrm{gt}_{\m}(I)$, i.e., once Golodness is achieved, it cannot be lost. In the last section, we work in the setting of a regular local ring of dimension 3, and show that the product of any two proper ideals is Golod; this resolves a question posed by Dao and De Stefani \cite[Question 4.5]{dao2022monomial} and VandeBogert \cite[Question 4.11]{vandebogert2022products}.

papers.name: Spectra of gcd-graphs over a matrix ring
papers.abstract: In this short note, we calculate the spectra of gcd-graphs defined over a matrix ring. Using character sums, we show that this calculation can be reduced to certain counting problems. In particular, when the underlying ring is a matrix ring with coefficients in a finite field, we calculate these spectra explicitly. We will also show that two gcd-graphs over the same matrix ring are isospectral if and only if they have the same generating set.

papers.name: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, Θ)$ satisfies that $I_X(2Θ)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebro-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

papers.name: Congruence density under sublattice inclusion
papers.abstract: Following Gábor Czédli, the \emph{congruence density} of a finite lattice $A$ is $\cd(A)=|\Con A|/2^{|A|-1}$, where $\Con A$ is its congruence lattice and $|A|$ is its number of elements. Czédli proved that density cannot increase under several kinds of sublattice extension and asked whether this holds for every sublattice inclusion. For a sublattice $S$ of $L$, we prove the stronger inequality $\cd(L)\leq2^{-d}\cd(S)$, where $d$ is the larger of the increases in the numbers of join-reducible and meet-reducible elements. The proof follows congruence labels along the chains into which prime intervals of $S$ split in $L$. We also prove that $\cd(L)=\cd(S)$ if and only if every element of $L-S$ is comparable with every element of $L$. The theorem of G. Czédli and L.~Szabó relating compatible quasiorders to pairs of congruences gives the corresponding quasiorder-density results.

papers.name: Integral Exponential Series: Fibonacci Weights and Implicit Equations
papers.abstract: We apply classical prime-power congruence criteria to two families of exponential series. For the Fibonacci numbers $F_n$, we characterize the polynomials $P\in\Z[T]$ for which $\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}P(F_n)x^n/n)$ has integer coefficients: this holds if and only if $P$ is even and $P(0)\equiv P(1)\equiv P(2)\pmod5$. In particular, $5$ is the least positive multiplier for each positive even power of $F_n$, and the series with weights $5F_n^{2k}$ has degree $5^{k-1}$ over $\Q(x)$ for $k\ge1$. For $R_n(y)\in\Z[y]$ satisfying $R_{pn}(y)\equiv R_n(y)\pmod p$ for every prime $p$ and every $n\ge1$, we prove that $H(x,y)=\exp(\sum_{n\ge1}R_n(y)^n x^n/n)$ belongs to $\Z[y][[x]]$ and that $A(x)=H(x,A(x))$ has a unique integral solution. For $q\in \Z$, taking $R_n(y)=q^n+y$ proves the conjecture in OEIS A163138; the Fibonacci result proves the conjecture in A207969 and A207970. For the implicit family with indeterminate $q$, the coefficient of $x^n$ has degree $n^2$, leading coefficient $1/n$, and nonnegative integer coefficients in the binomial basis, for every $n\ge1$.

papers.name: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.name: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
papers.abstract: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.

papers.name: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.name: Higher derived limits, Kurepa families and Chang's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between homological algebra and combinatorial set theory, specifically focusing on the (non)vanishing of higher derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups, denoted $\mathbf C_{[κ]^λ}$, indexed by the ordered sets $([κ]^λ,\subseteq)$, where $λ< κ$ are infinite cardinals. Our first main result is a general structural theorem which provides a generalisation of Goblot's theorem to the setting of locally small directed sets. We then present the first systematic study of generalised cofinal Kurepa families. We establish their existence in the constructible universe $L$ and under specific cardinal arithmetic hypotheses. Then, we apply our structural result to show that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} = 0$ in environments where the appropriate cofinal Kurepa families exist. In contrast, we explore conditions that force these derived limits to be nonzero. In particular, we prove that certain instances of Chang's conjecture (CC), together with the existence of suitable $\diamondsuit$ sequences, imply that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$ for appropriate values of $κ$. Adapting forcing techniques from Eskew and Hayut, we construct models of these instances of CC together with the required $\diamondsuit$ sequences, establishing the consistency, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\aleph_{ω_n}]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$.

papers.name: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.name: Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikvári proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$. In this paper, we prove that graphs with minimum degree at least $n/3$ $(n\geq7)$ satisfy $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$. We also construct a counterexample to the conjecture. We therefore further study the enumeration of spanning forests in general graphs, proving an upper bound in terms of the degree sequence and characterizing the extremal graphs attaining this bound. In addition, using the matrix-forest theorem, we obtain an upper bound for the number of spanning forests of a connected graph in terms of its algebraic connectivity, and characterize the extremal graphs attaining this bound.

papers.name: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
papers.abstract: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $α$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, Córdoba--Martínez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.

papers.name: On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
papers.abstract: For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.

papers.name: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
papers.abstract: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslantμ_2/(μ_n-δ)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $μ_2$ and $μ_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $δ$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.

papers.name: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

papers.name: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
papers.abstract: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},Σ},U_n^\mathrm{ét}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{ét}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric étale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $Σ$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

papers.name: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
papers.abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

papers.name: On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes

papers.name: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
papers.abstract: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.

papers.name: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
papers.abstract: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem. We bring new insight on this question for outerplanar graphs, whose WL-dimension is $2$. We show that color refinement, i.e. 1-WL, distinguishes connected rooted outerplanar graphs: two non-isomorphic such graphs receive different stable colorings once a single vertex, the root, is individualized. The root is necessary, as there are non-isomorphic $2$-connected outerplanar graphs that color refinement does not distinguish. Our result extends to pseudo-rooted graphs, in which the stable coloring merely contains a singleton color class, and to non-connected graphs whose components all contain such a class. Consequently, the $(1,1)$-WL test of Rattan and Seppelt (2023) distinguishes all outerplanar graphs. We proceed by inversion: we reconstruct a connected rooted outerplanar graph, up to isomorphism, from its color graph, the weighted quotient of the graph by its stable color classes, together with its root color. The reconstruction runs in time linear in the output size and is canonical, which yields a near-linear-time canonization algorithm for these graphs. Our main tool is a dichotomy lemma, formalized in Rocq: in a rooted outerplanar graph with an equitable coloring, every block either receives pairwise distinct colors or admits a color-preserving mirror symmetry fixing its vertex closest to the root.

papers.name: On Zhao's conjectural basis for finite multiple zeta values
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture by J. Zhao which states that every finite multiple zeta value associated with a nonempty index is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(k_1,\dots, k_r, 2, 1)$, where $k_i\in \{2, 3\}$. Our proof proceeds by constructing a basis for the space of formal multiple zeta values defined by the confluence relations. This approach also reduces the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture (apart from compatibility with the depth filtration) to linear independence conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values, without using motivic theory.

papers.name: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve. We use the theory of BPS Lie algebras, their $χ$-independence property (proven by Kinjo-Koseki), the recent proof of the stack version of $P=C$ due to Picovschi and Davison's analytic neighborhood theorem to reduce the conjecture to a comparison problem between (the 'pure' part) of the BPS Lie algebra asociated to the stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve and the BPS Lie algebra of the stack of representations of the preprojective algebra of the quiver $S_g$. This last step is taken care of by a quiver analog of Markman's tautological generation theorem for the BPS Lie algebra of arbitrary quivers (this last result is also proven by Davison and Hennecart).

papers.name: A proof of the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture on entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We complete the Eskenazis--Nayar--Tkocz conjecture: among the one-dimensional projections of the uniform measure on a cube, differential entropy is maximized precisely in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. Pang proved the conjecture in every dimension at least $150$. We prove the remaining dimensions using polynomial entropy bounds in dimensions three through six and exact certificates for derivatives of the logarithm of the diagonal projection density. The proof uses integer arithmetic and certified one-dimensional integration. We also derive quantitative stability estimates and determine the optimal asymptotic coefficient of a linear stability bound. The source code and the outputs of all finite verifications accompany the paper.

papers.name: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two. The same holds for ergodic planar billiards with piecewise C2 boundary, such as the Bunimovich stadium, the Sinai billiard, and generic polygons. The proof combines the Fourier analysis in the fibers with holomorphic functions on the transport twistor space. As a consequence, on these surfaces and on the Bunimovich stadium, a high-energy sequence of normalized Laplacian eigenfunctions tends to be equidistributed in the phase space if and only if it tends to be equidistributed in the physical space. In particular, on every stadium, every failure of equidistribution in the phase space implies scarring in the physical space. Combined with Hassell's theorem, this gives a new proof of scarring in the physical space for almost every stadium. In higher dimensions, we obtain an entropy bound for the ergodic components of such measures. We also construct counterexamples for hyperbolic toral automorphisms.

papers.name: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields. Similar results may be possible for other problems in analytic number theory.

papers.name: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+5e/2$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

papers.name: Discrete Hyperbolic Cosecant Distributions
papers.abstract: We introduce three families of discrete hyperbolic cosecant probability distributions, supported either bilaterally on $\mathbb{Z}$ or unilaterally on $\mathbb{N}_0$, inspired by series evaluations of Srinivasa Ramanujan. We determine their exact normalization constants in terms of singular values of complete elliptic integrals and the Gaußian constant $G=\varpi/π$ with the lemniscate constant $Γ^2(1/4)/(2\sqrt{2π})$ by explicitly calculating some series, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{κ\in \mathbb{Z}} 2κ\operatorname{cosech}(κπ) = G^2 + \frac{1}π. $$ Furthermore, by connecting these distributions to Fourier transforms of powers of the hyperbolic secant and applying the Poisson summation formula, we obtain closed-form evaluations for even moments and hyperbolic secant lattice sums, e.\,g. $$ \sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \mathrm{sech}^4(k π) = \frac{2}{3} \left(G^4 + G^2 + \frac{1}π\right). $$ This machinery proves conjectures on lattice sums arising in electrostatics proposed by Vigren and Dieckmann (Symmetry, 2020).

papers.name: Odd-degree cycles and rationality of Peskine sixfolds of discriminant 24
papers.abstract: Benedetti and Faenzi conjectured that, for a general trivector $σ\in\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$, the Peskine sixfold $X_1^σ$ is rational if the Brauer class $β$ on the associated K3 surface vanishes. We prove this implication for every $σ$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset $U\subset\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$. When $β=0$, we construct a line on the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration after a cubic field extension and use odd-degree descent to obtain a line over the original function field. We extend criteria for rationality to smooth complete intersections of an arbitrary number of quadrics under suitable hypotheses. Finally, we describe the derived category of the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration in terms of a twisted nodal curve of arithmetic genus two.

papers.name: A Fast and Accurate Time-Space Decomposition for Unit Commitment With Storage
papers.abstract: Grid-scale batteries couple decisions across time. This makes unit commitment (UC) with thousands of buses, batteries, generators, and alternating current constraints intractable. We introduce a time-space decomposition (TSD) heuristic to solve the problem. We first calculate target net battery charge or discharge rates on a zonal level, relaxing spatial constraints. We then incorporate this target into the Relax-and-Round UC (RRUC) solver from our previous work. RRUC enforces the spatial transmission constraints and transfers power between zones, if that reduces costs. We show that our TSD produces an error of about 0.1% on a simpler economic dispatch problem with batteries. This is larger than the error produced by RRUC in the tests in our previous work. So, we conjecture that the combined error of our two approximations is not much larger than 0.1%. We show that TSD with RRUC can solve systems with 10,000 buses in about 6 minutes, with sub-quadratic scaling, making it suitable for real time operations on an ISO-sized system.

papers.name: On stretched Kostka polynomials
papers.abstract: Stretched Kostka polynomials are defined by $f_{λ,μ}(N) := K_{Nλ,Nμ}$, where $K_{λ,μ}$ denotes the corresponding Kostka number. In 2004, King-Tollu-Toumazet conjectured that, for every integer $k$, there are only finitely many polynomials $f_{λ,μ}(N)$ such that $f_{λ,μ}(1)=k$. For $k=3$, KTT also conjectured that there are exactly two such polynomials. We prove both conjectures via Ehrhart theory, by counting lattice points in families of rational polytopes with a fixed set of normals.

papers.name: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
papers.abstract: We prove Schlösser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

papers.name: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
papers.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $β>β_c$ and logarithmically fast when $β<β_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $β$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $β$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $β$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

papers.name: High-dimensional limit theorems for adaptive variants of SGD I: Ballistic limits
papers.abstract: We develop the high-dimensional effective dynamics for adaptive, momentum-based variants of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). These effective dynamics are given by a Markov process. They key observation is that the non-Markovianity in the algorithm due to the exponential moving average and preconditioning can be treated using the method of averaging. Our approach applies to a broad class of algorithms including to Adaptive momentum estimation (ADAM), Momentum orthogonalized by Newton-Schultz (MUON), and its variants. It also applies to a broad class of learning tasks, such at tensor PCA, Gaussian projective models, teacher-student networks, and a multi-layer neural network trained on the XOR problem using a hybrid of MUON and ADAM as commonly done in practice. We demonstrate how to this technique can give precise, quantitative comparisons between algorithms. In particular, we find interesting phenomena, such as the cross-over phenomenon where online SGD has better generalization than ADAM early in training until the learning curves cross and ADAM dominates. Furthermore, we prove a version of the Edge of Stability phenomenon. In particular, we introduce an analogue of the infinity Laplacian that sharply characterizes the Edge of Stability.

papers.name: Log-optimal two-sample testing by betting
papers.abstract: For each standard Borel observation space, we construct a single anytime-valid two-sample procedure that is asymptotically log-optimal for every pair of unknown probability laws and every limiting ratio of diverging sample sizes, including zero and infinity. For independent balanced pairs, the optimal log-wealth rate is $2\JS(P,Q)$, where $\JS$ is the Jensen--Shannon divergence. Unequal sizes yield weighted Jensen--Shannon information and the one-sample limit $\log W(n_1,n_2)/n_2\to\KL(Q\|P)$ when $n_1/n_2\to\infty$. Refining finite partitions and logarithmic-loss learning with measurable characteristic kernels provide universal constructions. Our main contribution is the generality of our construction, and its connections to classical batch efficiency notions. Practical implementations allow continuous classifier fine-tuning, as demonstrated on finite alphabets, Gaussian data, and handwritten digits.

papers.name: Classification of critical points of heat kernels on flat tori and Riemann theta functions
papers.abstract: For any two-dimensional flat torus $E_τ:=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathbb Zτ)$ and any $t>0$, we prove that the heat kernel $p_τ(z,t)$ has either four or six critical points on $z\in E_τ$ (i.e., including four trivial critical points and at most one pair of nontrivial critical points). This is interestingly consistent with Lin-Wang's remarkable result (Ann. Math. 2010) for the Green function. The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given.

papers.name: Stokes Waves in a Finite-Depth Fluid via a Conformal Transformation
papers.abstract: Euler equations for a spatially periodic surface in a two-dimensional fluid of a finite depth are reduced to a system of evolution equations after a conformal transformation. Compared to the previously developed formal approach, we show that the system of evolution equations is complemented by two constraints which determine the new depth in conformal variables and the Bernoulli integration constant. A locally unique continuation of the traveling Stokes waves with respect to the wave speed is studied by using arguments based on the implicit function theorem. We show that the constraints on the traveling wave profile recover the correct small-amplitude expansion of Stokes waves in physical variables. We also prove for the co-periodic stability problem that the real unstable eigenvalues may bifurcate from the zero eigenvalue only at a critical point of the wave energy. Finally, we perform numerical approximations of the wave profiles for both small and large amplitudes and illustrate different bifurcations along the solution family.

papers.name: Betti numbers of powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs
papers.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the Betti numbers of all powers of Ferrers ideals and edge ideals of threshold graphs.

papers.name: A proof of Schmeisser's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1977, Schmeisser proposed a strengthening of Sendov's conjecture: if all zeros of a polynomial $p$ of degree $n\ge2$ lie in the closed unit disk, then for every point $ξ$ in the convex hull of the zeros of $p$, there exists a critical point $ζ$ of $p$ such that $ |ξ-ζ|\le 1.$ We prove this conjecture in every degree. The proof combines a covering of the convex hull by diameter disks, inequalities for reflected polynomials, and quantitative estimates for centred products, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted verification in a finite range of degrees.

papers.name: On the Flucher--Rumpf isoperimetric question for the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem: a conformal reformulation, quantitative bounds and the second variation at the disc
papers.abstract: Let $c(Ω)$ be the Bernoulli constant of a bounded domain $Ω\subset\R^N$, that is, the infimum of the parameters $λ$ for which the interior Bernoulli free boundary problem $Δu=0$ in $Ω\setminus K$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, $u=1$ and $|\nabla u|=λ$ on $\partial K$ admits a classical solution. Flucher and Rumpf asked whether $c(Ω)\ge c(Ω^*)$, where $Ω^*$ is the ball of the same volume. The variational analogue was settled by Daners and Kawohl, but the variational constant differs from $c$ already for the ball, and the original question remains open. We prove the following. (i) Through a conformal parametrisation of $Ω\setminus K$ by an annulus, every classical solution in a simply connected planar domain with connected, filled free set satisfies $λ\geμ/R$, where $πR^2=|Ω|$ and $μ\approx 2.485268$; hence $c(Ω)\ge 0.9142\,c(Ω^*)$ for every bounded planar convex domain of class $C^1$. (ii) In this class, the Flucher--Rumpf inequality is equivalent to an area inequality for analytic functions in an annulus, which also provides an explicit generator of exact solutions. (iii) A Rellich--Pohozaev identity yields, in every dimension $N\ge2$ and for every strictly star-shaped domain, $c(Ω)\ge\max\{\sqrt{θ(Ω)},κ_N\}\,c(Ω^*)$, where $θ(Ω)\in(0,1]$ is an explicit geometric quantity equal to $1$ only for balls and $κ_N$ is an explicit constant with $κ_3\approx0.650$ and $κ_N\to1$ as $N\to\infty$.

papers.name: Stability of Self-Similar Expansions for Self-Gravitating Hyperelastic Bodies
papers.abstract: We consider the three-dimensional elastodynamics system with nonlocal gravitational coupling and nonlinear traction-free boundary conditions, modeling an isolated self-gravitating hyperelastic body, where the strain-energy function is assumed to be objective, isotropic, and homogeneous of degree $-1$. We prove nonlinear stability of a self-similarly expanding separable solution, recently constructed by the authors [JangLeslie2025], under radial perturbations satisfying the codimension-one constraint of zero total energy. Using a self-similar reformulation analogous to that developed for the mass-critical Euler--Poisson system in [HadzicJang2018CPAM], we recast the perturbed equation as a scalar nonlinear five-dimensional radial wave equation and the nonlinear traction-free boundary condition as a homogeneous Neumann condition. A key is to identify a quasilinear form of the leading-order spatial operator that is compatible with this boundary condition and yields coercive energy estimates. Our energy estimates capture the stabilizing effect of the background expansion and yield global existence and nonlinear codimension-one stability in self-similar variables.

papers.name: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

papers.name: NS-bialgebras, the NS-Yang-Baxter equation and dendriform D-bialgebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bialgebra theory for NS-algebras via the Manin triple approach. We first study representations of NS-algebras and establish an equivalence among NS-bialgebras, matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-algebras. We then introduce the NS-Yang-Baxter equation (NS-YBE) and show that its symmetric solutions induce triangular NS-bialgebras. We further investigate the relationship between symmetric solutions of the NS-YBE and $\mathcal O$-operators of NS-algebras, and characterize pre-NS-algebras in terms of invertible $\mathcal O$-operators. As an application, we investigate the relation between NS-bialgebras and dendriform D-bialgebras via double constructions of Connes cocycles. In particular, we show that every NS-bialgebra induces a dendriform D-bialgebra structure on the direct sum of two copies of its underlying vector space.

papers.name: The Contact Process with Temporary Immunity on $\mathbb{Z}$
papers.abstract: We develop a regeneration scheme for the one-dimensional contact process with temporary immunity, also known as the spatial SIRS process, a non-attractive interacting particle system. The key ingredient is a one-sided space-time shielding mechanism, constructed from infinite infection paths of an auxiliary process. These paths separate the evolution of the infection front from the configuration and graphical history left behind, allowing us to construct regeneration times without relying on attractiveness. The same shielding mechanism also provides coupling arguments for processes started from different initial configurations. Using this approach, we establish a law of large numbers and a functional central limit theorem for the right edge, existence and uniqueness of an invariant law for the process seen from the edge, and complete convergence. We also prove survival from every nonempty finite infected set for sufficiently large immunity-loss rates and derive an explicit extinction criterion.

papers.name: Pole rigidity in root-optimal rational approximation of the exponential on infinite sectors
papers.abstract: The optimal root convergence factor for uniform rational approximation of the exponential on an infinite sector is classical. We prove that, for every fixed infinite sector of opening less than $π$, the normalized pole-counting measures of any reduced root-optimal sequence, after scaling the poles by degree, converge weakly to a uniquely determined probability measure supported on a compact analytic arc outside the sector. For the half-line, the corresponding pole law was previously announced by Stahl and Schmelzer; our new result covers sectors of positive opening. The proof rules out boundary pole accumulation and controls an exponentially small Hermite residual through reflection and noncancellation, without assuming interpolation or orthogonality. We explicitly construct the equilibrium measure and its supporting arc in terms of a zero of a Ferrers function, and relate this parameterization to the Gonchar--Rakhmanov theta equation. We also obtain a degree-independent comparison for simultaneous approximation of finitely many $\varphi$-functions with a common denominator. Numerical pole distributions support the theoretical law.

papers.name: Psyquandle Fares
papers.abstract: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

papers.name: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
papers.abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order. This allows us to reduce the description of certain Bruhat intervals to that of the corresponding Iwahori intervals. We next give closed-form descriptions of all Iwahori intervals, using the quantum Bruhat graph (QBG). More precisely, we show that lower Iwahori intervals saturate pseudo-Weyl polytopes (that is, certain intersections of negative cones), and upper Iwahori intervals saturate certain unions of positive cones, with the cone points given by explicit formulae involving paths in the QBG. We then describe arbitrary Bruhat intervals by partitioning them into their core, a large region which is (in most cases) completely determined by an Iwahori interval, and their crust, the complementary boundary region. We conclude by proving that, under a super-regularity assumption, the crust is covered by certain locally-defined tesselating shapes. All statements and proofs are rank- and type-free.

papers.name: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

papers.name: Classification of ${\rm GL}_1(D)\times {\rm GL}_{n-1}(D)$-distinguished representations
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a quaternion division algebra over a non-Archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. We prove the conjecture of Dagar, Sharma, and Verma classifying irreducible smooth representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n-1}(D)$ for $n>2$. These are precisely the trivial representation and the irreducible normalized parabolic inductions $\one_{n-2}\timesτ$, where $τ$ is an infinite-dimensional irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(D)$ distinguished by $\mathrm{GL}_1(D)\times\mathrm{GL}_1(D)$. The proof combines a choice of cuspidal inducing factor with orbit conditions and multisegment methods.

papers.name: Normalized ground states of Kirchhoff equation on waveguide manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the nonlinear Kirchhoff equation on the waveguide manifolds $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n$: \begin{align*} -\left( a+b \int_{\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{T}^n}|\nabla_{x,y}u(x,y)|^2\,dxdy\right) Δ_{x,y}u+ωu=|u|^αu, \end{align*} where $a,b>0$, $ω\in \mathbb{R}$, $α\in(0,2^*)$. We first establish existence of the normalized ground states when $α\in(0,2^*)$. To precisely characterize the $y$-dependence of ground states, we apply a scaling argument to handle the integral term $ \int_{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{T}^n} |\nabla_{x,y} u(x,y)|^2 dxdy$.
